title: Network
intro: AIODOS connects everyone's machines over the Internet, strangers on the public network included, to pool their computing power. For now, the public network is a directory: only your friends and your paired machines (pairing confirmed on both sides) compute for each other.
invitation_received: Invitation from “{name}” accepted {ago}: pairing will start once your friend has pasted your reply.
invitation_answered: Reply from “{name}” received: pairing in progress.
invitation_sent: Invitation created {ago}, waiting for your friend's reply (valid until {until}).
internet_off: Off: your machines only reach each other on the local network.
internet_denied: relay {relay} refuses this machine: its key must be on the relay's allowlist
internet_title: Connect my machines over the Internet
invite_hint: To pair the machine of a friend who isn't on your network. Create an invitation and send them the code (message, email); they paste it into their AIODOS with “Reply to an invitation”, then send you back their reply, which you paste here. You then each confirm the same 6-digit code. An invitation works only once, for 24 hours, and both sides need the Internet connection turned on.
copy_key_title: For the allowlist of a self-hosted relay (docs/relais.md)
copy_failed: Couldn't copy: select the code and copy it by hand.
invitation_title: Invitation to send to your friend
invitation_text: Send this code to your friend (message, email). They paste it into their AIODOS, then send you back their reply: paste it here, with “Paste the reply”.
invitation_copied: Invitation copied: send it to your friend.
accept_text: Paste here the invitation code you received from your friend.
reply_text: Send this reply back to “{name}”. Once they have pasted it, a pairing request will show up here: check together that you both see the same 6-digit code.
reply_copied: Reply copied: send it back to your friend.
paste_text: Paste here the reply your friend sent back to you.
paste_check: Check with your friend (by phone, by message) that they see this same code, say what their machine is to you, then each confirm on your own side.
public_needs_internet: First turn on “Internet”, just below: the public network goes through it.
public_none: No other public node online for now.
public_help: A directory with no owner (the BitTorrent DHT), where AIODOS nodes find each other without an invitation. This machine joins it with a separate key, which doesn't link it to your paired machines, and through the relays: your IP address isn't given to strangers, but a stranger running their own relay could see it (a known limit of this trial). It only tells its AIODOS version and the models it can compute. Nothing is entrusted to strangers, and nothing is computed for them: that will come later, with your consent.
local_off_internet: No more discovery or direct path on your network: your paired machines are still reached over the Internet.
local_off_nothing: Nothing leaves this machine. Turn on the local network or the Internet to pair it with your other machines.
local_visible_discovery: This machine (“{name}”) is visible on your network, port {port}, automatic discovery on.
local_visible: This machine (“{name}”) is visible on your network, port {port}.
add_hint: A machine on your network doesn't show up in “Detected machines”? Add it by its IP address.
firewall_html: When you turn it on, Windows will probably ask for firewall permission for Python: allow it for private networks only.
friend_profile: reduced profile (this machine counts you among its friends)
introduced_by_removed: introduced by a machine since removed

shared_size.one: Entrusted to this machine: {n} file or page ({size}), the last one {ago}
shared_size.other: Entrusted to this machine: {n} files or pages ({size}), the last one {ago}

shared.one: Entrusted to this machine: {n} file or page, the last one {ago}
shared.other: Entrusted to this machine: {n} files or pages, the last one {ago}

consulted: Searched your libraries: {facts}, the last one {ago}
offload_on: Your tasks can be handed to them.
offload_off: You don't hand your tasks to them.
peers_hint: Your machines and your friends'. Exchanges are encrypted, and each machine applies its own sharing rules (set in “This machine”). A friend only receives the libraries shared with your friends. {offload} A friend's machine also meets your other machines, and theirs meet yours, with your mutual agreement.
intro_waiting: introduced by “{presenter}” {ago} · waiting for your answer
introduced_title: Paired through an introduction: no code to compare, the trust comes from the machine that introduced it
set_aside_text: Set aside {ago}: {reason}. Nothing is entrusted to it anymore.

working_for_me.one: Computing for you right now: {n} unit
working_for_me.other: Computing for you right now: {n} units

ledger_chats: Conversations served by a lent model: {received} for you · {given} for it
show_shared: See what was entrusted to it
show_consulted: See its searches in your libraries
unpair_friend_text: “{name}” will no longer be able to exchange with this machine. Your other machines will remove it too, unless you tick the box below. You'll have to pair again to get it back.

unpair_introduced_text.one: “{name}” will no longer be able to exchange with this machine. It introduced {n} friend's machine to you ({names}): if it is lost or stolen, remove that one too, from all your machines.
unpair_introduced_text.other: “{name}” will no longer be able to exchange with this machine. It introduced {n} friends' machines to you ({names}): if it is lost or stolen, remove them too, from all your machines.

unpair_with_introduced: Also remove the friends' machines it introduced
unpair_text: “{name}” will no longer be able to exchange with this machine. You'll have to pair again to get it back.

unpair_missed.one: Offline, will be notified when it's back: {names}.
unpair_missed.other: Offline, will be notified when they're back: {names}.

offline_hint: Offline: check that it is on and that AIODOS is running on it, on the same Wi-Fi as this machine, with no VPN blocking the local network (in NordVPN, for example: allow the local network).
offline_hint_peer_internet: Offline: check that it is on and that AIODOS is running on it, on the same Wi-Fi as this machine, with no VPN blocking the local network (in NordVPN, for example: allow the local network); to reach it over the Internet, “Internet” must also be turned on there.
offline_hint_internet: Offline: check that it is on and that AIODOS is running on it, on the same Wi-Fi as this machine, with no VPN blocking the local network (in NordVPN, for example: allow the local network); or turn on “Internet” above, to reach it even outside the local network.
present_none: No other machine of yours to introduce.
trust_friend_done: “{name}” is now a friend's machine: only the libraries shared with your friends will be entrusted to it.
trust_mine_done: “{name}” is now one of your machines: full trust.
shared_text: The files and pages whose processing was entrusted to it, newest first (right of the arrow, the name it received them under).
consulted_text: Its searches in the libraries you open to it, newest first, with the documents the passages it received come from. Its questions are not kept.
visible_off: Turn on the local network to see the other AIODOS machines on your network (over the Internet: “Invite a friend” or one of your machines, above).
visible_hint: The AIODOS nodes announcing themselves on your network. If a machine doesn't show up, add it by its IP address in “Local network”.
pairing_waiting: waiting for confirmation on the other machine
trust_mine_help: Full trust: all your libraries can be computed there, except those kept on this PC.
trust_friend_help: Only the libraries shared with your friends, under neutral file names; its results are spot-checked.
pair_check: Check that this same code shows on the other machine, say what it is to you, then confirm here AND there.
details_internet: It is reached over the Internet, by invitation.
details_known: Warning: “{name}” is already paired with this machine; accepting will replace its key. If nothing changed on it (reinstall, pairing removed on its side), decline.
details_crowd: Warning: another pairing request is open at the same time. If you were expecting only one machine, decline everything and start over: someone else may be trying to pair.
codes_match_replace: The codes match: replace its key
confirmed_here: Confirmed here. Now confirm on the other machine.
intro_text: “{presenter}” is introducing “{machine}”, another machine belonging to the same person. If you accept, it will be able to exchange with this machine like “{presenter}”, at the same trust level, without a code to compare.
intro_always: Automatically accept the next machines of this group
request_text: “{name}” wants to pair with this machine. Accept only if this same code shows on its screen, and say what it is to you.
